_rationale.ladder: Escalation follows measured sensitivity, not intuition. Three components are intolerant at INT8 and are held at BF16 in every tier: H0 (10.09% worst-QP penalty), H3 (38.15%) and D5 (8.06%). The ladder varies only the four encoder DCB blocks, which hold 84.7% of all parameters and 41% of kMAC/px, so they decide both size and risk.
_rationale.entropy_frozen: The entropy components H0-H3 stay at 16-bit and are frozen during fine-tuning. The released bundle ships precomputed integer CDF tables in entropy_control_int.pt; changing those weights would invalidate the bit-exact coding contract. Keeping them fixed is what makes the QAT checkpoint safe to decode.
_rationale.train_scope: backbone = encoder and decoder weights. The entropy model and the QP controls are frozen.
_rationale.tier1: Control. The validated post-training optimum at a 1% worst-QP budget. QAT must not make it worse; if it does, the fine-tuning recipe is wrong.
_rationale.tier2: The realistic win. All four encoder blocks move to INT8, which is 3.50% predicted penalty before any recovery, to check whether QAT can bring 84.7% of the parameter mass to 8 bits. Target size about 15.8 MB.
_rationale.tier3: The frontier. The four encoder blocks drop to 4-bit with group-32 scaling (5.0 effective bits per weight, versus 8.03 for INT8). Per-channel INT4 measured 148-3767% penalty; group-32 cuts the weight error 32% versus per-channel. Target size about 11.3 MB. Expected to fail recovery, which is itself the finding.
